original_question: Does there exist an integer D such that every 2-degenerate graph G with Delta(G) > D satisfies chi(G^2) <= 5 Delta(G) / 2? More generally, does there exist an integer D such that every graph G with Delta(G) > D and maximum average degree mad(G) < 4 also satisfies chi(G^2) <= 5 Delta(G) / 2?
target_in_paper: Section 3.3, Questions 24 and 25, posed immediately after Theorem 23 in the discussion of graph classes with bounded maximum average degree.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the core mathematical content of the paper-faithful open problems: the coefficient 5/2, the two graph classes involved (2-degenerate graphs and, more generally, graphs with mad(G) < 4), the large-maximum-degree threshold, and that the parameter being bounded is the ordinary chromatic number of the square chi(G^2), not a neighboring parameter such as clique number or a generic linear bound.
missing_details: The survey states this as two separate open problems, Question 24 and Question 25, rather than as a single merged question.
The paper's threshold is Delta(G) >= D, not Delta(G) > D.
If one combines the two parts into one statement, the threshold constants should be allowed to differ; the paper asks for an integer D separately in each question.
To be stand-alone, G^2 should be defined as the graph on V(G) in which two vertices are adjacent exactly when their distance in G is at most 2.
To be stand-alone, chi(G^2) should be identified as the ordinary chromatic number of the square.
To be stand-alone, mad(G) should be defined as max_{H subseteq G, |V(H)| >= 1} 2|E(H)|/|V(H)|.
To be stand-alone, 2-degenerate should be defined, e.g. every nonempty subgraph has a vertex of degree at most 2.
The ambient setting is graph-theoretic: finite simple graphs. No ring/field, homogeneity, or nilpotency assumptions are relevant here.
refined_question: The paper actually asks the following two-part open problem: Do there exist integers D1 and D2 such that, for every finite simple graph G, (i) if G is 2-degenerate and Delta(G) >= D1, then chi(G^2) <= (5/2)Delta(G); and, more generally, (ii) if mad(G) < 4 and Delta(G) >= D2, then chi(G^2) <= (5/2)Delta(G)? Here G^2 is the square of G, obtained by joining pairs of vertices at distance at most 2 in G, chi(G^2) is its chromatic number, and mad(G) := max_{H subseteq G, |V(H)| >= 1} 2|E(H)|/|V(H)|.
justification: The nearest official formulation in arXiv:2210.05915 is not a conjecture labeled in the introduction, but the pair of open problems Question 24 and Question 25 in Section 3.3 (p. 17). Your draft is very close to those statements: Question 24 asks whether there exists an integer D such that every graph G with Delta(G) >= D that is 2-degenerate satisfies chi(G^2) <= 5Delta(G)/2, and Question 25 asks the analogous broader question for graphs with mad(G) < 4 (Section 3.3, Questions 24 and 25, p. 17). To make the problem fully stand-alone, the notation must be imported from the introduction: chi^2(G) means the chromatic number of the square G^2, and G^2 is formed by adding edges between pairs of vertices at distance at most 2 in G (Section 1, pp. 2-3); mad(G) is defined as the maximum average degree over subgraphs (Section 1, p. 3). The coefficient 5/2 is exactly paper-faithful: immediately before Questions 24 and 25, the survey explains that Charpentier's earlier 2Delta conjecture is false and then gives Theorem 23, which provides a lower-bound construction showing the naturality of the 5Delta/2 target (Section 3.3, pp. 16-17). The only substantive mismatch in your draft is precision: the paper uses Delta(G) >= D rather than Delta(G) > D, and it poses the two cases as separate questions rather than one single statement with a common D.
